thread.title: Amazon Smart-Home Devices With Alexa Arrive | Investor's Business Daily

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: Amazon Smart-Home Devices With Alexa Arrive | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Amazon ( AMZN ) on Thursday announced a bevy of new products that expands its line of Echo smart speakers and connections to smart-home devices, all controlled via the artificially intelligent Alexa.
X
Smart speakers, such as the Echo line of products, are becoming the central communication hub of smart homes. The e-commerce giant is in a race with Google-owner Alphabet ( GOOGL ) to lead the market.
New smart-home devices include a microwave with an "Ask Alexa" button that pairs with an Echo device. The AmazonBasics Microwave includes dozens of quick-cook voice presets, controlled by Alexa. It will cost $59.99 and ships later this year.
The company also introduced Alexa Guard. It integrates Echo devices, smart lights and security service providers to help customers protect their homes while they're away. If an Echo device in the home detects an unusual sound, such as breaking glass, it will inform the user.
 Amazon introduced various other products for home security and protection. Several of them integrate with its recent acquisition, Ring. In February, Amazon bought Ring , the maker of a smart doorbell that streams audio and video to smartphones, for a price reportedly above $1 billion . With Ring and a series of smaller acquisitions and organic initiatives, Amazon has built out its smart-home footprint.
Amazon Smart-Home Enhancements Other new smart-home devices enable users to lock or unlock their home using a smartphone app.
Amazon also unveiled a new version of the Echo Dot, its least expensive smart speaker. The new Echo Dot is 70% louder than the current version. Amazon also introduced a totally new product called Echo Input. It does not have a speaker, but users of the device can connect it to other speakers via Bluetooth. It then functions just like Alexa.
Other products include Alexa Connect Kit, which is used for creating Wi-Fi-connected smart-home products. Amazon also introduced an upgraded version of the Echo Show, an Alexa-enabled device with a monitor. The new version has a screen twice as large as the older version, with increased resolution and sound.
Amazon leads the smart-speaker category , with 70% market share in the U.S. Google Home is second, with a 24% share. Apple ( AAPL ) is third at 6%, with its Apple HomePod.
Also joining the market for smart speakers is Sonos ( SONO ), which recently held its initial public offering . Sonos stock fell to a record low as the Amazon products were introduced.
Alexa was initially used for common things like playing music, keeping lists and answering questions. It since has become a smart-home utility. Amazon is spending millions on improving Alexa's list of applications, which it calls skills.
Shares of Amazon closed at 1,944.30, up 0.9% on the stock market today .
